Greg Casar

Democratic candidate for U.S. Representative, District 37, Travis County, Texas · Open seat

U.S. Representative (TX-35); Chair, Congressional Progressive Caucus

Greg Casar is a Democrat who has represented Texas's 35th Congressional District since January 2023. Before that, he served on the Austin City Council from 2015 to 2022. Texas redrew its congressional map, and the new TX-35 no longer includes Austin, so he is running in District 37, the seat long held by Rep. Lloyd Doggett.

Where Casar stands

Affordability / cost of living
Says affordability would be his top priority. Proposes a 10-part "New Affordability Agenda" with caps on utility bills, childcare costs, and grocery and prescription drug prices.
Utility bills
Proposes capping utility bills as part of his New Affordability Agenda.
Consumer pricing / data privacy
Supports a bill to ban surveillance pricing, meaning charging customers different prices based on their browsing history and personal data.
Energy / gas prices
Supports a windfall profits tax on oil companies and a rebate for Americans who he says are overpaying for gas.
Artificial intelligence / campaign money
Opposes federal preemption of state AI rules and spending by AI-industry super PACs. Says "The people are beating back the money."

Background

  • U.S. Representative, Texas 35th District, 2023–present
  • Chair, Congressional Progressive Caucus, 2025–present
  • Austin City Council, District 4, 2015–2022
  • Born in Houston in 1989 to Mexican immigrant parents
